ChromeOS has a major limitation in that it can run much less apps than any of the other operating systems. But it still seems to be popular. Gartner is predicting 7.3 million units will be sold in 2015. Why are people buying these - as opposed to running Windows/Linux and only using the browser? Wouldn't this provide more flexibility?

The link you referenced pretty much spells it out for you--they are being used for education. This makes perfect sense. It is pretty hard to fuck up a chromebook through software and I am sure there are guest/parental controls that can be added on top of the chromeos 'sandbox.'

But seriously though, it's great for porn.

It is pretty hard to fuck up a chromebook through software

That's true. On the ChromeOS subreddit, the only malware anyone there ever caught was a malicious Chrome extension installed by Windows malware that hopped over to the Chromebook from Chrome syncing their extentsions.

The lack of flexibility is a feature, not a bug. Sometimes you just want a terminal, and in those cases the cost in complexity of a highly mutable operating system only gives you potential headaches and security vulnerabilities.

Here are two use cases where I found Chrome OS to be the best choice:

  1. My personal laptop. I spend a lot of my free time screwing around with programming projects, and for these I have a reasonably powerful Xeon workstation running Linux, which I can access remotely over SSH or Chrome Remote Desktop. I previously used a Mac as my main laptop, but for anything beyond browsing the web I'd wind up SSHing to my workstation (my "real" computer).

    So why spend time properly administering two general-purpose operating system installations when I only need one? With Chrome OS I never have to deal with a dozen App Store updates when I start the computer for the first time in weeks, or failed OS updates rendering the device unusable.

  2. My mom's computer. She was spending all her time in the browser anyway. She uses many different applications—all web-based. Why should she deal with the downsides of a Windows computer if the hypothetical upsides are of no value to her?
